content:
I'll fully admit that my DIY iPhone camera hack looks pretty silly — but it's genuinely made my iPhone photography more practical and more enjoyable.

It started as a solution I came up with for a specific video shoot, but unexpectedly, I've found myself reaching for it time and time again...

In the world of compact cameras, one of the biggest divides has been whether or not to include a viewfinder. Camera enthusiasts of old would have heated arguments about electronic viewfinders (EVF) versus optical ones, but electronic viewfinders are now so good that very few people care anymore.

But whether optical or electronic, a viewfinder offers some very practical advantages over composing with the rear screen, especially when shooting in harsh sunlight. Even at maximum brightness, when the sun is blazing down it's still very difficult to see what you're shooting, and reflections on the screen also cause problems.

While in London this has historically not been a major issue, this summer has brought record-breaking heatwaves, and honestly, I feel like the last time I saw a cloud or rain was about thirty years ago.

But for me, it means more than that. There's a psychological difference between seeing the framed image through a viewfinder versus seeing everything around you when shooting with the rear screen. Sometimes that's exactly the feeling that makes me choose a standalone camera over my iPhone.

When I was choosing a camera for videography a few years ago, the Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 4K was a clear standout winner, but the lack of a viewfinder did give me pause. In the end, I decided it wasn't a major issue for me, because I primarily use it indoors, and when I need to use it outside, attaching a large display with a sun hood solves most of the problems.

However, there are times when I want to operate in a more compact form factor rather than hauling the whole rig with display attached, so I found a simple accessory designed for outdoor use. It's a combined shading and magnification accessory that magnetically attaches to the camera's rear display, effectively providing an optical viewfinder experience.

I had an upcoming shoot where I needed to record with both the BMPCC 4K and my iPhone 16 Pro Max. I did a quick test run at the location, and the viewfinder accessory really came in handy. Since the BMPCC 4K and iPhone displays are similar in size, I wondered if I could use it on the iPhone too.

Of course there's no magnetic attachment, but the iPhone is light enough that holding it against the magnifier isn't an issue at all. To my surprise, it worked remarkably well, especially when I used the Camera Control button as a shutter release.

Since then, I've used this accessory in numerous shooting situations, enjoying both the clearer screen visibility in harsh sunlight and that sense of immersion. My iPhone has long been my go-to camera, and with this DIY modification, I find that even more often, just bringing my phone along is sufficient.

Ridiculous, or genius? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments. If you think it's genius, unfortunately the product I bought appears to be discontinued, and I haven't yet seen similar products designed for screens larger than three inches. If you find one, be sure to drop a link in the comments.
